newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods steady, but weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods steady, but weakness seen.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices held steady after a weak morning session, traders said Tuesday, but players saw futher weakness with the return of a key jet fuel unit and rising gasoline inventories.
Jet fuel prices, which registered strong gains last week, held at 80.50/82 cents a gallon after losing a half cent this morning.
The arrival of jet fuel imports and the return of ARCO's 4,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) hydrocracker near Los Angeles, weighed on West Coast distillates, traders said.
"The diesel will start to come off," a broker said.
CARB diesel cargoes ranged between 85 and 87 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, flat from late Monday and off from a high last week of 88 cents for offers.
By posting the 88 cent price last week, West Coast CARB stood higher than other world markets, traders said, and stirred speculation of imports from the U.S Gulf.
Prices for low sulphur diesel in L.A. and the San Francisco held at 76/77 cents after dropping a cent earlier.
Conventional gasoline prices in both cities were unchanged late at 74/75 cents a gallon.
CARB gasoline sold for 79.75 cents a gallon, trader said.
But prices were seen easing after the American Petroleum Institute, a oil industry trade group, reported West Coast gasoline inventories rose 612,000 barrels last week.
"If anything, that's bearish for gas," a broker said.
